inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026E = 9M FY26 actual 44,523 (Q1 14,438 + Q2 14,408 + Q3 15,677, 10-Qs) + Q4 FY26E ~15,850 (+8% y/y on Q4 FY25 14,639; Q3 was +12.5% y/y with Personal Systems +18% on units -16%, i.e. memory-cost pass-through pricing). FY0 is FY2026E because the year ends 2026-10-31, three quarters are reported and Q4 is guided; the projection starts FY2027.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 901.8M basic on the 10-Q cover at 2026-08-19 (dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding) plus ~8M dilutive effect (Q3 FY26 weighted diluted 927M vs basic 919M). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, and the count is actually being funded down by buybacks ($300M / 12.2M shares in Q3 FY26, $725M 9M FY26).
inputs.balance_sheet_note: 2026-07-31 (Q3 FY26 10-Q, filed 2026-08-27): cash and equivalents 4,169; long-term debt 7,868 non-current + 1,292 current = 9,160 (XBRL LongTermDebtNoncurrent + LongTermDebtCurrent; DebtCurrent 1,292 ties). Gross cash per release 4.2B incl. 3M short-term investments. Operating lease liabilities (~1.2B) are NOT in net debt because the lease cost sits inside EBITDA under US GAAP.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: FY2026 guidance midpoint (raised 2026-08-26 to $3.0-3.2B; HP definition = OCF less net PP&E/purchased intangibles less net investment in integrated-financing leases). 9M FY26 actual 2,454 (150 + 756 + 1,548). Reported FCF is POST interest paid (~$437M FY25, InterestPaidNet); the component build below is unlevered and deducts net debt, so year-1 component FCF sits above last_fcf by roughly after-tax interest. FY26 also carries ~$0.19/share (~$0.2B) of one-off tariff refunds, which is why the FY27 margin path starts below the FY26 print.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY25 interest income 89M (InvestmentIncomeInterest) is NOT stripped: HP carries net DEBT of ~5.0B, so there is no double-counted cash pile. Interest income sits inside 'interest and other, net' with the larger interest expense.
inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL ShareBasedCompensation (cash-flow add-back): FY24 452, FY25 522, 9M FY26 389 -> FY26E ~520 (Q4 ~130). HP publishes no combined SBC-plus-withholding figure and does not tag PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation; the add-back is used alone, so the true equity cost is understated by any net-share-settlement withholding.
inputs.buyback_note: Actual financing outflow, 9M FY26 (PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock): Q1 325, Q2 100, Q3 300. FY25 850, FY24 2,100. Dividends 825 9M FY26 ($0.30/qtr).
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD discount rate. 10y UST ~4.2% + beta 1.1 x 5.0% ERP = 9.7% cost of equity; pre-tax cost of debt ~4.6% (FY25 interest 430 on ~9.6B) -> 3.8% after tax at 18%; market weights ~75% equity (28.5B) / 25% debt (9.2B) -> 8.2%, used as 8.25%. Cyclicality is carried in beta and in the scenario spread, not as an ad-hoc premium; WACC is identical across scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP ASC 842 operating leases: lease cost (~$256M cash payments FY25) is inside operating expense and therefore inside EBITDA; lease liabilities excluded from net debt; lease_cost_pct_path 0. One treatment, applied once.
inputs.nci_treatment: None material; net earnings are fully attributable.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing: US operating company, hardware OEM). House basis expenses SBC and holds the count flat. No Analysis JSON existed for HPQ at build time, so business context comes from the Q3 FY26 release (8-K ex-99.1 2026-08-26), the 10-Q and the 2026-09-21 Reg-FD 8-K (industry PC units expected down mid-single-digits in CY2027; no FY27 guidance yet). Segment picture Q3 FY26: Personal Systems 11.8B (+18% y/y, units -16%, 4.6% op margin), Printing 3.9B (-2%, supplies -3%, 18.1% op margin). EBITDA in this model is GAAP operating income + D&A + SBC, i.e. restructuring (233/327/222 in FY24/FY25/9M FY26) is left inside as a recurring cost; amortization of acquired intangibles (~300/yr, Poly) is inside D&A. Interim CEO (Bruce Broussard) since Q2 FY26 - CEO transition costs are in 'other charges'. Price is a regular-session close, not after-hours.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: long-run revenue ~1%/yr (5yr revenue CAGR -0.5% FY20-FY25; FY26E +9% is memory-cost pass-through pricing on falling units, not volume growth). Equity CAGR unavailable: book value has been negative since FY2016 (buybacks in excess of earnings; -346 at FY25).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR undefined (negative book value FY16-FY25). EPS 5yr CAGR (+5.8%) exceeds revenue (-0.5%) because of the share count falling 1,420M -> 953M; owner-FCF 5yr CAGR is -8.0% vs reported -5.6%: SBC grew 278 -> 522 while FCF shrank, so a rising share of reported cash flow is paid out in stock.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC; interest income not stripped, net-debt company): FY20 3,458; FY21 5,497; FY22 3,355; FY23 2,540; FY24 2,705; FY25 2,278; FY26E 2,580. FY21 was a pandemic PC peak.

base.narrative: FY27 revenue -3%: industry PC units down mid-single-digits (HP's own 2026-09-21 planning assumption) partly offset by mix/pricing, Printing -2% with supplies -3%. Thereafter 1-2% as commercial AI-PC refresh and WXP/Poly offset print decline. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin starts at 7.6% (FY26E 7.8% less ~0.35pt of one-off tariff refunds) and recovers to 8.0% as memory costs normalize and Future Ready savings land, still below the FY21-24 9-10% band because Personal Systems margin (4.6% in Q3) does not fully recover. Cash tax ramps 17% -> 20% (FY24/FY25 cash taxes were 20% of pretax). Capex 1.3% (FY25's 1.6% was elevated; 9M FY26 590). Negative-working-capital business, so the FY27 decline consumes cash. Cap 12x.

bull.narrative: Commercial AI-PC refresh and Windows 10 end-of-support tail keep Personal Systems growing through the CY2027 industry dip; memory/storage costs ease and pricing holds, lifting PS margin back toward 6%; Printing stabilizes on Big Tank/subscriptions and commercial graphics so supplies decline slows to low-single-digits; WXP (Poly) and services grow double digits. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin returns to the FY21-24 9-10% band (9.5%). Cap 14x, terminal growth 2%.

bear.narrative: FY26 was a price-driven peak: PC units fall mid-single-digits in CY2027 AND memory-cost pricing unwinds, so revenue falls 7% then 3%; tariff refunds do not repeat and new tariff rounds are absorbed rather than passed on; Printing supplies decline accelerates to mid/high-single-digits as the installed base shrinks; the interim-CEO period stalls Future Ready execution. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin settles at 6.5% (PS ~3.5%, Print ~16%). Long-run growth 0.5%, cap 10x, terminal growth 1%.

scenario_narratives.base: HP is a two-engine business: a low-margin (4-5%) Personal Systems franchise of ~$45B and a ~$16B Printing franchise whose ~18% margin rests on a structurally shrinking supplies annuity. FY26 revenue (+9%) is price, not volume: Q3 PS units were -16% while revenue was +18% as memory and storage costs were passed through. The base case takes HP's own planning assumption (industry PC units -MSD in CY2027) as FY27 -3%, recovers the pre-SBC EBITDA margin to 8% (not the 9-10% of FY21-24), keeps restructuring inside the cost base because HP restructures every year, and caps the exit at 12x owner FCF, roughly today's EV/FCF.
scenario_narratives.bull: The commercial AI-PC refresh cycle and Windows 10 end-of-support carry PS through the industry unit dip; component costs ease while pricing holds; Print stabilizes; Future Ready delivers its cost target under a permanent CEO. Margin returns to the FY21-24 band and the market grants a 14x exit.
scenario_narratives.bear: The FY26 price-driven peak reverses on both units and price; supplies decline accelerates; tariffs are absorbed; leadership transition drags. HP still generates cash (bear owner FCF ~ $1.8-2.0B) but at a 10x exit and 6.5% margin the equity is worth well under the current price.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25% (up from the 15% house default): FY26 is a price-inflated base, HP itself flags CY2027 industry PC units down mid-single-digits, printing supplies are in structural decline, and the CEO seat is interim. Bull 25% (down from 35%): the bull case needs three independent things (AI-PC cycle persistence, memory-cost relief with pricing held, print stabilization) to land together. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value HP as a mature, cash-generative hardware OEM in mild structural decline, on fully SBC-expensed owner FCF with a flat share count, unlevered flows discounted at a USD WACC and net debt of ~$5.0B deducted. The FY26 revenue base is treated as a cyclical/pricing peak, not a growth inflection; the terminal multiple is capped at or below today's EV/FCF so no multiple expansion is assumed.
key_risks_to_valuation: PC unit cycle: HP's own planning assumption is industry units -MSD in CY2027; a deeper correction after the Windows 10 / AI-PC pull-forward is the bear axis.
Memory/storage cost pass-through: FY26 revenue growth is price; if component costs fall and pricing follows, revenue deflates with no margin gain.
Printing supplies annuity (~18% segment margin, the majority of group operating profit) declining 3-4%/yr with the installed base; acceleration is not in the base case.
Tariffs: FY26 EPS includes $0.19 of one-off refunds; future tariff rounds may be absorbed rather than passed on.
Leadership: interim CEO since Q2 FY26; Future Ready cost programme execution risk.
Balance sheet: $9.2B gross debt against negative book equity; buybacks are discretionary and were cut to $850M in FY25.
SBC understated: no equity-award tax-withholding figure is disclosed, so the house basis is slightly generous.
